classification.difficultyReason: Part h requires identifying that the circumference angle determines a reflex central angle, converting to the minor and then adjacent central angle, and completing a tangent-radius right triangle.

spec.description: Tangent and centre-crossing secant; centre is marked without a printed O.
spec.mathematics: External angle 25 degrees; a is the supplementary centre angle toward the far circumference endpoint.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 25 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The radius is perpendicular to the tangent.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-25^\circ\\\theta&=65^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-65^\circ\\a&=115^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ is the centre angle facing the external point.

spec.description: Horizontal diameter and left vertical tangent, with sloping secant through O.
spec.mathematics: 73-degree centre angle; a is the exterior angle between the downward tangent continuation and upward secant.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 73 degrees and exterior unknown a only.

answer.worked:
Vertically opposite centre angles are equal. The tangent is perpendicular to the horizontal radius.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-73^\circ\\\theta&=17^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-17^\circ\\a&=163^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ is the interior angle at the external point.

spec.description: Lower-left external point, upper-left tangent contact, and secant through an unnamed marked centre.
spec.mathematics: External angle 24 degrees; upper-right inscribed angle a lies between the chord and secant.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 24 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-24^\circ\\\theta&=66^\circ\\\phi&=180^\circ-66^\circ\\\phi&=114^\circ\\a&=\frac{180^\circ-114^\circ}{2}\\a&=33^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ faces the external point at the centre and $\phi$ faces the upper-right endpoint. The triangle formed by the two radii is isosceles.

spec.description: Vertical diameter extended below the circle and tangent to the lower-right contact; top 31-degree label has a leader.
spec.mathematics: Top radius–chord angle 31 degrees; external angle a.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 31 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The triangle formed by the two radii is isosceles.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-2(31^\circ)\\\theta&=118^\circ\\\phi&=180^\circ-118^\circ\\\phi&=62^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-90^\circ-62^\circ\\a&=28^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ is the centre angle facing the top endpoint and $\phi$ faces the external point. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.

spec.description: Tangent from an upper-right point, centre-to-external-point line through the upper-right circumference endpoint, and two chords from the left endpoint.
spec.mathematics: Left inscribed angle 32 degrees subtends the arc between the upper-right radial endpoint and tangent contact. The external angle a is between the tangent and line to O.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 32 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=2(32^\circ)\\\theta&=64^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-90^\circ-64^\circ\\a&=26^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact.

spec.description: Bottom horizontal tangent, external-to-centre line crossing the lower-left circumference, and separate chords to the upper-right point.
spec.mathematics: External angle 38 degrees; a at the upper-right circumference subtends the lower-left-to-bottom arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 38 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-38^\circ\\\theta&=52^\circ\\a&=\frac{52^\circ}{2}\\a&=26^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc.

spec.description: Tangent at the upper-left contact and external-to-centre line through the right circumference point; two chords meet at the left point.
spec.mathematics: External angle 18 degrees; left inscribed angle a subtends the tangent-contact-to-right-endpoint arc.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 18 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-18^\circ\\\theta&=72^\circ\\a&=\frac{72^\circ}{2}\\a&=36^\circ\end{aligned}$$
The angle at the circumference is half the angle at the centre on the same arc.

spec.description: Lower-left external point, upper-left tangent contact, centre-crossing secant, and top inscribed vertex.
spec.mathematics: Top inscribed angle 122 degrees subtends the major arc; a is the exterior-point angle between tangent and secant.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 122 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The reflex angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=360^\circ-2(122^\circ)\\\theta&=116^\circ\\\phi&=180^\circ-116^\circ\\\phi&=64^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-90^\circ-64^\circ\\a&=26^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ is the smaller centre angle between the two upper endpoints and $\phi$ faces the external point. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.

spec.description: Right vertical tangent extending upward, secant through O to the lower-left endpoint, and chord to the tangent contact.
spec.mathematics: Lower-left radius–chord angle 30 degrees; external angle a.
spec.answerVisibility: Given 30 degrees and unknown a only.

answer.worked:
The triangle formed by the two radii is isosceles.
$$\begin{aligned}\theta&=180^\circ-2(30^\circ)\\\theta&=120^\circ\\\phi&=180^\circ-120^\circ\\\phi&=60^\circ\\a&=180^\circ-90^\circ-60^\circ\\a&=30^\circ\end{aligned}$$
Here $\theta$ faces the lower-left endpoint at the centre and $\phi$ faces the external point. The tangent is perpendicular to the radius.
